purpose: First real cross-dataset comparison (BioUnlearn-Bench vs TOFU) for the paper's core diagnostic claim

RMU.note: much more aggressive than GA/NPO at the same dose

RMU_RGU.note: see RGU_rmu_pilot_summary.json -- essentially no movement, gentlest of the three

KEY_FINDINGS: 1. GA's catastrophic collapse is NOT BioUnlearn-Bench-specific -- the exact same failure mode (model_utility/retain-quality crashing to near-zero) occurs on TOFU too at aggressive (many-step) settings, confirming this is a general GA property, not a clinical-domain-specific problem.

2. At a properly-tuned, non-collapsed, matched dose, all three methods (GA/NPO/RMU) produce real, non-degenerate forgetting on BOTH datasets -- both datasets have a usable 'sweet spot' operating range.

3. RMU's relative gentleness is NOT a fixed property of the method. On BioMistral-7B, RMU was the gentlest of the three at matched doses (near-zero movement). On TOFU (Llama-3.2-1B) and on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (a separate earlier cross-model test), RMU was MORE aggressive than GA/NPO, sometimes dramatically so. This is a genuine, reportable methodological finding: relative baseline-method rankings depend on model architecture, not just the method itself -- a paper claiming 'method X is gentler than method Y' needs to qualify this per-model.

4. IMPORTANT GAP NOT YET CLOSED: this comparison shows the methods behave similarly in terms of collapse-vs-non-collapse tradeoffs across datasets, but does NOT yet test the paper's core, more specific diagnostic claim -- that clinical concepts' ontological entanglement (a forgotten fact sitting one hop from many retain-critical neighbor concepts) causes COLLATERAL damage that TOFU's independent, unrelated fictitious facts structurally cannot show. TOFU has no analogous 'neighbor concept' structure to test OCD-style collateral damage against. This remains the load-bearing comparison still needed, not yet run.
